study_identification_part.si4_title: A normative modelling approach reveals age-atypical cortical thickness in a subgroup of males with autism spectrum disorder

dc1_datasets_using_in_this_study.answer: ABIDE I/II cortical thickness dataset (post-QC matched autism and TD groups)
dc1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: Final normative modelling sample after matching and QC: 699 autism participants and 624 typically developing controls (male), with cortical thickness extracted from ABIDE I/II
dc1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: "Table 1 Sample age characteristics... Autism | ... N | 699 ... TD | ... N | 624"
dc1_datasets_using_in_this_study.location: Bethlehem2020.pdf.md: Table 1 Sample age characteristics after normative modelling selection

dc2_purpose_of_each_dataset.answer: TD group used to build age-based normative CT models; autism group used for individualized deviation (w-score) mapping
dc2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: Male TD data provided age-binned normative means/SDs via LOESS; ASD participants were scored against these norms to identify regional age-atypical cortical thickness and outlier prevalence
dc2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: "Normative modelling of age-related CT effects was done utilizing male-only data from the typically developing group... For each age bin and every brain region we computed a normative mean and standard deviation from the TD group... the normative mean and standard deviation are used to compute a w-score for each individual with autism"
